createSingleGeneEffectMap()[source]

This takes a model and analyses the logical gene expression patterns. This only needs to be done once, the result is a dictionary that has boolean effect patterns as keys and the (list of) genes that give rise to those patterns as values. This map is used by the single gene deletion method for further analysis.

Note this dictionary can also be stored and retrieved separately as long as the model structure is not changed i.e. the gene associations themselves or order of reactions (stored as the special entry ‘keyJ’).

Stored as self.__single_gene_effect_map__

cbmpy.CBRead.readSBML3FBC(fname, work_dir=None, return_sbml_model=False, xoptions={'validate': False}, scan_notes_gpr=True)[source]

Read in an SBML Level 3 file with FBC annotation where and return a CBM model object.

Parameters:

  • fname – is the filename

  • work_dir – is the working directory

  • return_sbml_model – deprecated and ignored please update code

  • xoptions – special load options, enable with option=True except for nmatrix_type which has a type.

  • nmatrix_type – [default=’normal’] define the type of stoichiometrich matrix to be built

cbmpy.CBRead.readExcel97Model(xlname, write_sbml=True, sbml_level=3, return_dictionaries=False)[source]

Reads a model encoded as an Excel97 workbook and returns it as a CBMPy model object and SBML file. Note the workbook must be formatted exactly like those produced by cbm.writeModelToExcel97(). Note that reactions have to be defined in both the reaction and network_react sheets to be included in the model.

Parameters:

  • xlpath – the filename of the Excel workbook

  • return_model – [default=True] construct and return the CBMPy model

  • write_sbml – [default=True] write the SBML file to fname

  • return_dictionaries – [default=False] return the dictionaries constructed when reading the Excel file (in place of the model)

  • sbml_level – [default=3] write the SBML file as either SBML L2 FBA or SBML L3 FBC file.

Takes the resuls of a FluxVariabilityAnalysis method and writes it to a nice csv file. Note this method replaces the glpk/cplx_WriteFVAtoCSV methods. Data is output as a csv file with columns: FluxName, FVA_MIN, FVA_MAX, OPT_VAL, SPAN

  • roundec – [default=None] an integer indicating at which decimal to round off output. Default is no rounding.

  • scale_min – [default=False] normalise each flux such that that FVA_MIN = 0.0

  • appendfile – [default=False] instead of opening a new file try and append the data

  • info – [default=None] a string added to the results as an extra column, useful with appendfile

Split a single reversible reaction into two irreversible reactions.

Splits a reversible reaction (A = B) into two irreversible reactions: - Forward: A -> B - Reverse: B -> A

The original reversible reaction and its bounds are deleted from the model.

  • fba (CBMPy model) – an instantiated CBMPy model object

  • rid (str) – a valid reaction ID

  • fwd_id (str, optional) – the new forward reaction ID (defaults to rid + ‘_fwd’) [default=None]

  • rev_id (str, optional) – the new reverse reaction ID (defaults to rid + ‘_rev’) [default=None]

Returns:

tuple – (original_reaction, lower_bound, upper_bound, equality_bound)

  • fba (CBMPy model) – a CBMPy model instance

  • items (str or list, optional) – what to check: ‘all’ means ‘species,reactions,flux_bounds,objectives’ [default=’all’]

Returns:

dict – a dictionary of errors found for each item type

cbmpy.CBTools.checkFluxBoundConsistency(fba)[source]

Check flux bound consistency for the model.

Check for multiply defined bounds, bounds without a reaction, inconsistent bounds with respect to each other, and reaction reversibility.

Parameters:

fba (CBMPy model) – a CBMPy model instance

Returns:

dict – a dictionary of errors found: - ‘eq+lb’: equality + lower bound conflicts - ‘eq+ub’: equality + upper bound conflicts - ‘duplicate_ids’: duplicate flux bound IDs - ‘multiple_defines’: multiple bound definitions - ‘lb>ub’: lower bound > upper bound - ‘undefined’: bounds without values - ‘rev_contradict’: reversibility contradictions - ‘no_reaction’: bounds without a reaction

cbmpy.CBTools.roundOffWithSense(val, osense='max', tol=1e-08)[source]

Round a value with sense-aware rounding.

Round a value in a way that takes into consideration the sense of the operation that generated it (maximize rounds up, minimize rounds down).

Parameters:

  • val (float) – the value to round

  • osense (str, optional) – the operation sense (‘maximize’ or ‘minimize’) [default=’max’]

  • tol (float, optional) – the tolerance for roundoff [default=1e-8]

Returns:

float – the rounded value

cbmpy.CBTools.mergeGroups(m, groups, new_id, new_name='', auto_delete=False)[source]

Merge a list of groups into a new group.

Merge a list of groups into a new group. Note: annotations are not merged.

Parameters:

  • m (CBMPy model) – a model containing the source groups

  • groups (list) – a list of group IDs to merge

  • new_id (str) – the new merged group ID

  • new_name (str, optional) – the new group name (default merges old names) [default=’’]

  • auto_delete (bool, optional) – if True, delete source groups after merge [default=False]

Returns:

bool – True if merge succeeded, False otherwise

cbmpy.CBTools.merge2Models(m1, m2, ignore=None, ignore_duplicate_ids=False)[source]

Merge two models (m2 into m1) without model checking.

Merge 2 models, this method does a raw merge of model 2 into model 1 without any model checking. Component IDs in ignore are ignored in both models and the first objective of model 1 is arbitrarily set as active. Compartments are also merged and a new “OuterMerge” compartment is created.

In all cases, duplicate IDs are tracked and ignored, essentially using the object ID encountered first (usually that of model 1). Duplicate checking can be disabled by setting the ignore_duplicate_ids flag.

Parameters:

  • m1 (CBMPy model) – model 1 (target)

  • m2 (CBMPy model) – model 2 (source)

  • ignore (list, optional) – list of IDs to skip during merge [default=None]

  • ignore_duplicate_ids (bool, optional) – disable duplicate ID checking [default=False]

Note

In development - merging genes and GPRs.

Returns:

CBMPy model – the merged model
